newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli parliament moves to tighten hold on Golan.
newsitem.headline: Israeli parliament moves to tighten hold on Golan.

text.p: Israel's parliament on Wednesday took a preliminary step towards passing a law which opposition members said would make it virtually impossible to trade parts of the occupied Golan Heights to Syria for peace.

The legislation, which passed the first of three required readings by a vote of 43-40, would make approval of territorial concessions on the Golan conditional on the support of at least 80 legislators in the 120-seat Knesset.

"This means the government of Israel cannot conduct negotiations with Syria. This will lead to a greater break with Syria, I think to greater deterioration," opposition Labour party legislator Haim Ramon told Army Radio.
The last peace talks between Israel and Syria were held more than a year ago under the previous Israeli government led by the Labour party.

Syria demands full return of the Golan Heights, which Israel occupied in the 1967 Middle East war. The prior Israeli government said the scope of any pullback on the strategic plateau would match the depth of the peace achieved.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who cast his vote for the measure proposed by the nationalist Tsomet party, said it should not alarm anyone.

"Every decision on a peace settlement with Syria that has any sort of territorial component, a decision like that has to come to the people for their decision," Netanyahu said, implying the parliament vote held little meaning.

Netanyahu, who is on record opposing territorial compromise on the Golan, was echoing the policy of the dovish government he ousted in elections a year ago which had pledged to bring any final deal with Syria to public referendum.
"I think the Golan is very vital, it is an important territory, it is important to this government," he said.

A group representing 15,000 Israelis who have settled amidst 18,000 Druze on the heights said in a statement: "The parliament relayed a clear message to the Syrians and to the entire world that Israel is serious in its intention to ensure its continued sovereignty on the Golan."
Israel extended its laws to the Golan in 1981 in a move not recognised by the international community.
